s:
With reference to GST collections in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Net GST collection in October 2026 grew by 15.8%.
2. Gross GST collection in September 2026 was Rs 2,03,521 crore, up 14.7% year-on-year.
3. Gross GST collection in October 2026 was Rs 2.31 lakh crore, up 22.9% year-on-year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: net GST in October 2026 was Rs 2.03 lakh crore, up 25.6%; 15.8% was the growth of domestic collections. Note: Rs 2.03 lakh crore is the NET figure for October but the GROSS figure for September.

s:
Consider the following statements about GST growth in the southern States:
1. In September 2026 Telangana recorded the highest GST growth in the south (18%).
2. In September 2026 Andhra Pradesh recorded 11% GST growth.
3. In October 2026 Andhra Pradesh recorded the highest GST growth among southern States (+24%).
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh grew only 6% in September 2026; 11% was Kerala's growth.

s:
With reference to GST institutions in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The 57th GST Council meeting was scheduled for 12 September 2026, after a gap of more than a year.
2. The new GST Standing Committee (October 2026) has 12 States, of which 7 are permanent members.
3. Kerala is a permanent member of the new GST Standing Committee.
4. The 57th meeting recommended raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: only 5 States are permanent members; the other 7 seats rotate every two years. 3 is wrong: the permanent members are Karnataka, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

s:
Match List-I (GST feature) with List-II (Provision):
List-I | List-II
a. Constitution of the GST Council | i. 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016
b. Constitutional basis of GST | ii. Half of the members
c. Quorum of the GST Council | iii. Article 279A
d. Offences, prosecution and arrest | iv. CGST Act, 2017
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: GST Council - Article 279A; GST introduced by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016 (in force 1 July 2017); quorum - half of the members; offences, prosecution and arrest - CGST Act, 2017.

s:
Assertion (A): No decision of the GST Council can be passed without the support of the Centre.
Reason (R): In the GST Council the Centre's vote carries one-third weight and decisions need three-fourths of the weighted votes.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both true and R explains A: the States together hold only two-thirds of the weight, which is less than the three-fourths needed, so the Centre's one-third is always required.

With reference to PM-DHARA (Green Energy Corridor Phase-III), consider the following statements:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 30 September 2026.
2. It will evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy through the Intra-State Transmission System by FY 2032-33.
3. Its implementing agencies are the State Governments.
4. It is the first time a dedicated battery-storage component has been included in the Green Energy Corridor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the implementing agencies are the State Transmission Utilities, not State Governments.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding renewable-energy transmission and targets:
1. Green Energy Corridor Phase-II was implemented in 5 States.
2. India targets renewable-energy capacity of 500 GW by 2030.
3. India targets 900 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2035.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: GEC Phase-II covers 7 States - Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.

s:
With reference to the SME Growth Fund approved in October 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It carries a government commitment of Rs 10,000 crore and was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.
2. It makes direct equity investments mainly in micro enterprises.
3. It is an Alternative Investment Fund; AIFs are regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.
4. The Budget gave an extra Rs 2,000 crore to the Self-Reliant India Fund for micro enterprises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the fund is for viable small and medium enterprises, NOT micro enterprises (micro enterprises got Rs 2,000 crore via the Self-Reliant India Fund).

s:
Consider the following statements about ECLGS 5.0:
1. It is a loan-waiver scheme accessed through the Jan Samarth Portal.
2. It facilitates additional credit of up to Rs 2.55 lakh crore.
3. For scheduled passenger airlines the tenure is 5 years including a 1-year moratorium.
4. It is implemented by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company through Member Lending Institutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: it is a guarantee scheme, not a loan waiver (access is via the Jan Samarth Portal). 3 is wrong: airlines get 7 years including a 2-year moratorium; 5 years with a 1-year moratorium applies to MSMEs/non-MSMEs.

s:
Consider the following pairs (ECLGS phase / feature - Coverage):
1. ECLGS 1.0 (2020) - Aatmanirbhar Bharat package (COVID)
2. ECLGS 4.0 - Hospitals and oxygen facilities
3. ECLGS 5.0 - MSMEs only
4. ECLGS 5.0 guarantee cover for MSMEs - 90%
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: ECLGS 5.0 covers MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines. 4 is wrong: MSMEs get 100% cover; 90% is for non-MSMEs and airlines.

s:
With reference to the incentive scheme for domestic PNG connections (2026), consider the following statements:
1. It gives 200 SCM of domestic APM gas per incremental active, billed household PNG connection above target.
2. States were urged to cut the GST rate on natural gas to 5%.
3. It is expected to cut the payback period on a connection from about 10 years to about 3 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: natural gas is outside GST; States were urged to cut VAT on natural gas to 5%.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector:
1. Its pilot was launched on 31 May 2023 through PACS.
2. NABARD is its implementing agency.
3. Micro food-processing units are supported through convergence with PMFME.
4. The National Food Security Act, 2013, which the foodgrain stocks serve, covers about 80 crore people.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the implementing agency is the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC); NABARD only provides refinance.

s:
Consider the following statements about currency events in India:
1. The demonetisation of 8 November 2016 was announced by the RBI Governor.
2. The ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes of the Mahatma Gandhi Series lost legal tender in 2016.
3. The RBI announced the withdrawal of ₹2,000 notes on 19 May 2023; by 30 April 2026, 98.47% had returned.
4. The ₹2,000 note ceased to be legal tender after the withdrawal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: it was announced by PM Narendra Modi in a televised address at 8 pm. 4 is wrong: the ₹2,000 note remains legal tender.

s:
Assertion (A): The Reserve Bank of India is the sole note-issuing authority in India.
Reason (R): The design and production of currency notes are handled by the RBI alone.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: the RBI is the sole note-issuing authority. R is false: design and production of currency are shared by the RBI and the Government of India.

With reference to the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP), consider the following statements:
1. It is India's first collective domestic platform for insuring large maritime risks.
2. It is administered by the New India Assurance Company.
3. It covers only Indian-flagged ships.
4. Its first policy (12 May 2026) was issued by New India Assurance to Hoger Offshore and Marine Pvt Ltd.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the administrator is the General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re); New India Assurance only issued the first policies. 3 is wrong: it also covers vessels owned/managed by Indian entities and cargo to or from India.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool:
1. Its capacity is about Rs 13,906.50 crore (~USD 1.5 billion).
2. Claims up to USD 100 million are met from reserves/reinsurance; the sovereign guarantee applies only after reserves are exhausted.
3. It runs for 10 years, extendable to a maximum of 20 years.
4. It covers Hull & Machinery, Cargo War, Protection & Indemnity and War-perils risks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: it runs for 10 years, extendable to a maximum of 15 years.

Match List-I (Development, 2026) with List-II (Feature):
List-I | List-II
a. Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 | i. SEBI's 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' programme
b. NABKISAN Finance Ltd | ii. Replaced an Act of 1891
c. SBI 'CyRIS' | iii. India's first WASH Social Bond listed on the NSE
d. Project Jagruk | iv. Cyber Security Centre of Excellence in Mumbai
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 (in force 1 Oct 2026) replaced the 1891 Act; NABKISAN (a NABARD subsidiary) listed India's first WASH Social Bond on the NSE; SBI launched CyRIS in Mumbai (30 Oct 2026); 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' is SEBI's programme under Project Jagruk.

Consider the following statements about savings rates announced in 2026:
1. PPF carries 7.1% interest for October-December 2026.
2. Sukanya Samriddhi carries 8.2% interest for October-December 2026.
3. The small savings rates for October-December 2026 were cut by the Finance Ministry.
4. The EPF interest rate for 2025-26 is 8.25%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the rates for October-December 2026 were kept unchanged (30 Sep 2026).

With reference to the NPCI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for UPI, consider the following statements:
1. It is effective from 15 October 2026.
2. P2P, P2PM and AutoPay transactions attract an MDR of 0.4%.
3. Essential-sector payments of ₹2,000 or more attract a flat MDR of ₹5.
4. Merchant (P2M) payments above ₹2,000 attract an MDR of 0.4%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: P2P, P2PM and AutoPay carry Nil MDR; 0.4% applies only to merchant payments above ₹2,000.

s:
Assertion (A): From 15 October 2026, UPI merchant (P2M) payments above ₹2,000 attract an MDR of 0.4%, while UPI stays free for consumers.
Reason (R): Zero-MDR on UPI since January 2020 was provided under Section 10A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true: the NPCI framework (effective 15 Oct 2026) levies 0.4% on P2M payments above ₹2,000 and consumers pay nothing. R is false: zero-MDR since January 2020 was under Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

Consider the following statements about UPI in Uzbekistan:
1. NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL) tied up with Uzbekistan's National Interbank Processing Center (NIPC).
2. Uzbekistan became the 11th country to accept UPI, Bhutan being the first.
3. Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the world's two doubly landlocked countries.
4. Uzbekistan's capital is Tashkent and its currency is the Som.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All the statements are correct. Indians scan UZQR codes and pay from Indian bank accounts (1 Sep 2026).

List-I | List-II
a. NPCI set up in Mumbai | i. 2009
b. In-principle approval by RBI DPSS | ii. 2016
c. RuPay launched | iii. 2012
d. UPI launched | iv. 2008

x: NPCI was set up in 2008; RBI DPSS gave in-principle approval on 24 September 2009; RuPay was launched in 2012 and UPI in 2016.

Consider the following statements about the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI):
1. It was promoted by the RBI and the State Bank of India.
2. It is a not-for-profit Section 8 company under the Companies Act, 2013.
3. Its fast-payment platform is called 'Vajra'.
4. NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL) is its subsidiary taking UPI and RuPay abroad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: NPCI was promoted by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA).

With reference to the Global Fintech Fest 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Global Fintech Fest began in 2020.
2. The 2026 event was its 8th edition.
3. It was held at the Jio World Centre and Trident, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 2026 event (8-11 September) was the 7th edition. Organisers: Payments Council of India, NPCI and Fintech Convergence Council.

With reference to the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched on 13 October 2021.
2. Its GIS platform connects 58 Central Ministries and all 36 States/UTs.
3. Its nodal body is the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
4. The National Logistics Policy was launched on 17 September 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the nodal department is DPIIT.

Consider the following statements about India's steel sector:
1. The Draft National Steel Policy 2047 envisages crude steel capacity of 604 MT and exports of 45 MT.
2. The National Steel Policy 2017 set a target of 300 MT capacity by 2047.
3. The World Steel Association was established in 1967 and is headquartered in Brussels.
4. India is the second-largest steel producer after China.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: NSP 2017 targeted 300 MT by 2030-31; 2047 is the horizon of the new draft policy.

With reference to Make in India (12 years in 2026), consider the following statements:
1. India is now the largest mobile-phone maker in the world by volume.
2. It was launched on 25 September 2014 and is coordinated by DPIIT.
3. It covers 27 sectors - 15 manufacturing and 12 services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: India is the 2nd-largest mobile-phone maker by volume.

Assertion (A): The UP Cabinet's decision of 9 October 2026 by itself renamed the Noida (Jewar) airport as 'Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar'.
Reason (R): The final decision on naming the airport rests with the Union Cabinet followed by a Gazette notification.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: the UP Cabinet only proposed the name. R is true: the final decision needs the Union Cabinet and a Gazette notification.

Consider the following statements about India's largest phenol-acetone facility inaugurated in October 2026:
1. It is located at Paradip, Odisha.
2. It was built by Adperma Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Haldia Petrochemicals Limited.
3. It is the first phenol plant on India's eastern coast.
4. Phenol and acetone are produced together by the cumene process.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the plant is at Haldia, West Bengal (Purba Medinipur district).

List-I | List-II
a. National Strategic Trade Command Centre | i. Department of Commerce with DGFT
b. India Cine Hub | ii. Medical value tourism
c. Ramoji Film City (1996) | iii. National Film Development Corporation (NFDC)
d. Heal in India portal | iv. Hyderabad
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: NSTCC (Vanijya Bhawan) was developed by the Department of Commerce with DGFT; India Cine Hub is run by NFDC (1975); Ramoji Film City, Hyderabad dates from 1996; hospitals register on the Heal in India portal for medical value tourism (Sanjeevani-2026).

Consider the following statements about the 2026-27 Kharif sowing data (18 October 2026):
1. Paddy area fell by 15.56 lakh hectares.
2. Area under pulses fell by 2.57 lakh hectares.
3. Telangana recorded the biggest fall in paddy area.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: pulses area ROSE by 2.57 lakh ha, though other crops' net area fell by 11.81 lakh ha.

With reference to jute in India, consider the following statements:
1. The leading States in descending order are West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, Odisha and Jharkhand.
2. The Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987 mandates jute packaging for 100% of foodgrains and 50% of sugar.
3. The MSP of raw jute for 2026-27 is Rs 5,925 per quintal.
4. The Jute Corporation of India is the sole MSP agency for jute.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Act mandates 100% for foodgrains but 20% for sugar.

s:
Assertion (A): India launched the Grow More Jute Campaign in September 1949.
Reason (R): After Partition about 80% of the jute-growing area went to East Pakistan.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both true and R explains A: losing about 80% of the jute area to East Pakistan forced India to expand jute cultivation through the campaign (September 1949).

Consider the following statements about bamboo:
1. The National Bamboo Mission was launched in 2014-15.
2. After the 2017 amendment of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, bamboo grown on non-forest land is no longer a 'tree'.
3. Bamboo belongs to the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the National Bamboo Mission was launched in 2006-07 (restructured as a CSS from 2018-19).

With reference to India's fisheries sector, consider the following statements:
1. India targets 30 million tonnes of fish production in five years, up from 19.7 million tonnes.
2. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was launched in 2018.
3. The National Fisheries Development Board is headquartered in Visakhapatnam.
4. World Fisheries Day is observed on 21 November.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: PMMSY was launched in 2020. 3 is wrong: NFDB (est. 2006) is headquartered in Hyderabad.

With reference to the RBI monetary policy of 7 October 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The repo rate was raised by 25 bps from 5.25% to 5.50%.
2. It was the RBI's first repo hike since May 2022.
3. The stance was changed from 'Neutral' to 'Calibrated Tightening'.
4. The MSF rate and Bank Rate now stand at 5.75%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: it was the first repo hike since February 2023.

Match List-I (Provision / feature of the MPC framework) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. Section 45ZB of the RBI Act | i. Failure: 3 consecutive quarters outside the band
b. Section 45ZA of the RBI Act | ii. 6 members - 3 RBI and 3 Centre
c. Section 45ZN of the RBI Act | iii. Constitution of the Monetary Policy Committee
d. Strength of the MPC | iv. Inflation target of CPI 4% ± 2%

x: Section 45ZB creates the MPC; Section 45ZA provides the inflation target (4% ± 2%); Section 45ZN defines failure as 3 consecutive quarters outside the band; the MPC has 6 members (3 RBI + 3 Centre).

Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):
1. The inflation target is set by the RBI alone, every 3 years.
2. The RBI Governor has the casting vote.
3. The MPC was brought in by the 2016 amendment of the RBI Act, 1934.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the target is set by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI, every 5 years.

Consider the following statements about the RBI Greenfield Data Centre inaugurated on 25 October 2026:
1. It is located at Info Valley-II, Jatni, Khordha district, Odisha.
2. It is the backup and disaster-recovery centre for the RBI's main data centre in Chennai.
3. Its foundation was laid on 22 March 2023 by then Governor Shaktikanta Das.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the RBI's main data centre is in Navi Mumbai.

s:
With reference to CPI inflation for September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. All-India CPI inflation was 5.54%, above the 4% target but within the 2-6% band.
2. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest inflation among major States.
3. Tamil Nadu recorded 6.81%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Tamil Nadu (6.81%) was the highest; Uttar Pradesh was at 6.08%.

s:
Consider the following pairs (Data - Compiled by / Base year):
1. Wholesale Price Index - National Statistics Office
2. GDP estimates - National Statistics Office (MoSPI)
3. New CPI series - Base year 2012
4. Consumer Price Index - Labour Bureau
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
x: Pair 2 is correct. 1 is wrong: WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT. 3 is wrong: the new CPI series (released 12 Feb 2026) has base year 2024; 2012 was the old base. 4 is wrong: CPI is compiled by the NSO (MoSPI).

s:
With reference to the National Accounts Statistics 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was released by MoSPI on 31 August 2026 with 60 statistical statements.
2. The new base year is 2022-23, replacing 2011-12.
3. Real GDP is measured at current prices.
4. GDP = GVA + product taxes - product subsidies.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: real GDP is at constant prices; nominal GDP is at current prices.

s:
Assertion (A): The Finance Ministry's Monthly Economic Review for September 2026 estimated real GDP growth of 7.3% in Q2 (July-September) 2026-27.
Reason (R): The estimate came from a nowcasting model using high-frequency indicators, first presented in the Economic Survey 2026.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R only describes the method of estimation; the growth itself was driven by domestic demand and investment, so R does not explain A.

List-I | List-II
a. IMF (WEO, October 2026) | i. 7.3%
b. World Bank | ii. 7.0%
c. SBI Research | iii. 7.5%
d. Fitch BMI | iv. 7.1%

3. BMI, which raised India's forecast to 7.5%, is a division of Fitch Solutions.
4. The IMF cited domestic demand and services as India's growth drivers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the World Bank raised it from 6.6% (April 2026); 6.4% was the IMF's earlier figure.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the WEO is published twice a year, in April and October.

With reference to India's foreign-exchange reserves (RBI report, September 2026), consider the following statements:
1. The SDR component of the reserves is issued by the RBI.
2. India overtook Russia to rank 4th, with about USD 785.7 billion.
3. Switzerland ranks 3rd, ahead of India.

2. India has become a net exporter of pulses.
3. The GI-tagged Kalaburagi Tur Dal of Karnataka is in demand in the Maldives.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: India is still a net importer (~60 lakh tonnes a year) and is 1st in production, consumption and import of pulses.

3. Sagarmanthan was organised by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways with the Observer Research Foundation.
4. Sagarmanthan is linked to SDG 14: Life Below Water.

With reference to CPI inflation for October 2026 (released 12 November 2026), consider the following statements:

3. Onion showed the highest item-level inflation (116.22%).
4. Telangana recorded the highest headline inflation among major States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: Tamil Nadu (7.29%) was the highest; Telangana (7.26%) was second.

x: A is false: a single month above 6% is not a formal failure. R is true: under Section 45ZN, failure means three consecutive quarters outside 2-6%.
